materials.name: Shrinking-Violet Attar
materials.desc: A single bead of violet oil that visibly tightens the surface of whatever it touches. Diminution brewers treasure it because raw petals alone never hold the shrinking long enough.

recipe.lore: Six bushels of violets reduce to one drop; moonpetal keeps the fey virtue from fading, and quicksilver holds it in suspension.

materials.name: Unseen Distillate
materials.desc: A liquid you can only find by touch — the flask looks empty and casts no reflection. The heart of any true draught of invisibility.

recipe.lore: Glasswing nectar is only half-unseen; bleeding a stalker's core into it and straining it through shadowsilk finishes the job.

items.name: Potion of Healing
items.effect: A bright red tonic that knits flesh as it goes down, restoring 2d4 + 2 hit points.

recipe.lore: Every hedge-witch starts here: moss or silverleaf steeped in honeyed water, with yarrow to stanch the bleeding. The red colour comes from the yarrow, not magic — but customers expect it.

items.name: Potion of Greater Healing
items.effect: A deeper crimson draught that closes serious wounds, restoring 4d4 + 4 hit points.

recipe.lore: Mendwort teaches wounds to remember being whole; troll blood simply refuses to let them stay open. Either way, a base of healer's moss keeps the regrowth from running wild.

items.name: Potion of Superior Healing
items.effect: A glowing ruby elixir that restores 8d4 + 8 hit points, often mending broken bone outright.

recipe.lore: Kingsbalm and sunmend grow only where celestial light falls; a troll's heart or a hydra's regrowing flesh is the darker, cheaper road to the same miracle.

items.name: Potion of Supreme Healing
items.effect: Liquid sunrise in a phial: restores 10d4 + 20 hit points, enough to pull almost anyone back from the brink.

recipe.lore: The Everbloom root has never died once in its existence, and a planetar's tears fall only for the dying. Distilled over celestial dew, they carry that refusal into the drinker.

items.name: Potion of Hill Giant Strength
items.effect: For 1 hour your Strength score becomes 21 (no effect if it's already higher). The draught tastes of iron and the giant's homeland.

recipe.lore: Hill giant blood is thick, sour and stubborn; a knuckle of giant's-root and a splash of ogre blood coax it into a drinkable brew.

items.name: Potion of Frost Giant Strength
items.effect: For 1 hour your Strength score becomes 23 (no effect if it's already higher). The draught tastes of iron and the giant's homeland.

recipe.lore: The blood must never thaw fully — alchemists stir it over glacier ice from the giant's own stronghold so the strength doesn't bleed away as steam.

items.name: Potion of Stone Giant Strength
items.effect: For 1 hour your Strength score becomes 23 (no effect if it's already higher). The draught tastes of iron and the giant's homeland.

recipe.lore: Stone giant blood is half grit; it's settled for days with stoneroot until the sediment falls out and only the mountain's patience remains.

items.name: Potion of Fire Giant Strength
items.effect: For 1 hour your Strength score becomes 25 (no effect if it's already higher). The draught tastes of iron and the giant's homeland.

recipe.lore: Fire giant blood smokes in open air. Forge-ash from their own smithies and dragon's-blood resin keep it simmering without boiling off its might.

items.name: Potion of Cloud Giant Strength
items.effect: For 1 hour your Strength score becomes 27 (no effect if it's already higher). The draught tastes of iron and the giant's homeland.

recipe.lore: Cloud giant blood tries to rise out of the flask; a wisp of cloudstuff gives it somewhere to go, and the root anchors it to the drinker's sinews.

items.name: Potion of Storm Giant Strength
items.effect: For 1 hour your Strength score becomes 29 (no effect if it's already higher). Faint lightning crawls under the skin while it lasts.

recipe.lore: Storm giant blood alone is too wild to hold — it cracks the phial at the first thunderclap. Only a heart of the storm itself (eye-glass, an ancient blue's heart or a kraken's storm-organ) can master it.

items.name: Potion of Animal Friendship
items.effect: For 1 hour you can charm a beast of low intelligence as the animal friendship spell (DC 13), again and again.

recipe.lore: Beasts trust what smells like the forest itself. Living wood, a leaf that remembers being awake and honey make the drinker smell like a friendly grove.

items.name: Potion of Clairvoyance
items.effect: Drinking it grants the effect of the clairvoyance spell, letting you see or hear a familiar place far away.

recipe.lore: An eye that has seen across centuries or dimensions still wants to look further; eyebright and an eagle's eye point it where the drinker chooses.

items.name: Potion of Climbing
items.effect: For 1 hour you gain a climbing speed equal to your walking speed and advantage on climbing checks. The liquid is layered brown, silver and grey.

recipe.lore: Gecko-footed lizards and spiders never slip; boiled with clingvine tendrils and a thumb of pine resin, the draught leaves your palms faintly tacky for an hour.

items.name: Potion of Diminution
items.effect: For 1d4 hours you shrink as if under the reduce effect of enlarge/reduce, no concentration needed.

recipe.lore: Violets that grow beside fey crossings shrink from footsteps; their attar teaches the drinker to do the same. A rat's tail is added by old tradition 'so you know where to hide.'

items.name: Potion of Flying
items.effect: For 1 hour you gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed and can hover. If it ends mid-air, you fall.

recipe.lore: Thistle and wind-seed want to drift; a cloud giant's blood or a feather from an angel's wing gives the drift direction and will. Always cork it upside down.

items.name: Potion of Gaseous Form
items.effect: For 1 hour you become a drifting cloud as the gaseous form spell; you can end it early as a bonus action.

recipe.lore: Vampires turn to mist when wounded and djinn are made half of wind; either remnant, boiled with cloud and mistcap, lets flesh remember how to be vapour.

items.name: Potion of Growth
items.effect: For 1d4 hours you swell as if under the enlarge effect of enlarge/reduce, no concentration needed.

recipe.lore: Giantcaps double in size overnight after rain; a pinch of giant's-root and a hearty tuber give the swelling bulk something to build on.

items.name: Potion of Heroism
items.effect: For 1 hour you gain 10 temporary hit points and are blessed as the bless spell, no concentration needed.

recipe.lore: Brewed from things that never flinch — a guardian naga's heart, a deva's essence, a sphinx's mane — with lionsmane and a lion's heart for the old-fashioned courage.

items.name: Potion of Invisibility
items.effect: You turn invisible, along with what you carry, for 1 hour; attacking or casting a spell ends it early. The flask looks empty but sloshes.

recipe.lore: The distillate does the vanishing; ghostpetal keeps the effect from fading at the edges, and a drop of octopus ink hides the drinker's shadow.

items.name: Potion of Mind Reading
items.effect: Grants the detect thoughts spell (DC 13) for its duration. The liquid holds a slowly turning pink cloud.

recipe.lore: An aboleth's brain still listens after death, and mindbloom opens only when someone near it is thinking hard. Both lend their eavesdropping to the drinker.

items.name: Potion of Poison
items.effect: Looks, smells and tastes like a healing potion. The drinker takes 3d6 poison damage, must save (DC 13 Con) or be poisoned, and suffers more damage each turn until it passes.

recipe.lore: The whole art is disguise: a real sprig of healer's moss masks the bitterness, red dye completes the lie, and the deathcap does the rest.

items.name: Potion of Acid Resistance
items.effect: For 1 hour you have resistance to acid damage. The liquid carries a hint of its source — you can usually tell which one it is by colour.

recipe.lore: A pitcher plant never dissolves in its own juices, and a black dragon's scales shrug off what it breathes. Ankheg shell is ground in for good measure.

items.name: Potion of Cold Resistance
items.effect: For 1 hour you have resistance to cold damage. The liquid carries a hint of its source — you can usually tell which one it is by colour.

recipe.lore: Frost lichen thrives on bare glacier; rendered with polar bear fat, it leaves a warmth in the belly that no blizzard can reach.

items.name: Potion of Fire Resistance
items.effect: For 1 hour you have resistance to fire damage. The liquid carries a hint of its source — you can usually tell which one it is by colour.

recipe.lore: Emberbloom flowers inside volcanic vents; with cooling aloe and ashlily it gives skin the stubbornness of a thing that grew in fire.

items.name: Potion of Force Resistance
items.effect: For 1 hour you have resistance to force damage. The liquid carries a hint of its source — you can usually tell which one it is by colour.

recipe.lore: A bronze dragon's repulsion gland pushes everything away; filings of star-iron and lodestone teach the drinker's body to push back against raw force.

items.name: Potion of Lightning Resistance
items.effect: For 1 hour you have resistance to lightning damage. The liquid carries a hint of its source — you can usually tell which one it is by colour.

recipe.lore: Shambling mounds drink lightning and grow stronger; brewers wind the vines around copper wire so the charge drains harmlessly into the flask.

items.name: Potion of Necrotic Resistance
items.effect: For 1 hour you have resistance to necrotic damage. The liquid carries a hint of its source — you can usually tell which one it is by colour.

recipe.lore: Mummies keep death at bay with their embalming resins; natron dries the rot out, and garlic is there because grandmothers insist.

items.name: Potion of Poison Resistance
items.effect: For 1 hour you have resistance to poison damage. The liquid carries a hint of its source — you can usually tell which one it is by colour.

recipe.lore: A vulture eats carrion without harm, an otyugh wallows in filth; their gut-fortitude plus wyrmbane and sage makes a stomach that refuses venom.

items.name: Potion of Psychic Resistance
items.effect: For 1 hour you have resistance to psychic damage. The liquid carries a hint of its source — you can usually tell which one it is by colour.

recipe.lore: Amethyst has guarded sleepers from nightmares for ages; ground with dust from drifting thoughts, it builds a quiet wall around the mind.

items.name: Potion of Radiant Resistance
items.effect: For 1 hour you have resistance to radiant damage. The liquid carries a hint of its source — you can usually tell which one it is by colour.

recipe.lore: Things that live in holy light must learn to bear it; couatl scale and halo-quartz carry that tolerance, while smoky quartz dims the glare.

items.name: Potion of Thunder Resistance
items.effect: For 1 hour you have resistance to thunder damage. The liquid carries a hint of its source — you can usually tell which one it is by colour.

recipe.lore: A creature that roars must not be deafened by its own voice; its roar-sac, steeped with hushmoss, lets the drinker weather a thunderclap.

items.name: Potion of Speed
items.effect: For 1 minute you are hasted as the haste spell, no concentration needed: faster, harder to hit, and with an extra action each turn.

recipe.lore: A marilith moves six arms faster than most move one; a sphinx's tear bends time outright. Quickthorn and quicksilver carry the haste into the blood — it wobbles in the flask like a nervous animal.

items.name: Potion of Water Breathing
items.effect: For 1 hour you can breathe underwater. The cloudy green fluid smells of the sea and holds a single drifting bubble.

recipe.lore: Gillweed grows its own gills in the tide; bladderwrack's air pockets and a pinch of sea salt help the drinker's lungs remember the trick.

items.name: Potion of Longevity
items.effect: Your physical age drops by 1d6 + 6 years (minimum 13). Each further dose risks a cumulative 10% chance of instead aging you 1d6 + 6 years.

recipe.lore: The ageless lotus has bloomed in the same season for a thousand years. Amber holds a moment still and the nautilus counts time in spirals — backwards, if you grind it right.

items.name: Oil of Etherealness
items.effect: Spend 10 minutes anointing yourself and for 1 hour you slip into the Ethereal Plane as the etherealness spell. Cloudy grey, it beads on the skin like quicksilver.

recipe.lore: Night hags use their heartstones to walk the Border Ethereal; dissolved with phase-spider silk and a ghost's ectoplasm, the heartstone's trick soaks into the skin.

items.name: Oil of Sharpness
items.effect: Coat one slashing or piercing weapon (or 5 pieces of ammunition) over a minute; for 1 hour it counts as a +3 magic weapon.

recipe.lore: A marilith's hand or a sphinx's claw remembers every cut it made. Mixed with diamond dust and adamantine filings, the oil hones any edge to a legendary bite.

items.name: Oil of Slipperiness
items.effect: Anointed, you gain the benefits of freedom of movement for 8 hours; poured on the ground it creates a grease slick for 8 hours instead.

recipe.lore: Shark liver oil never congeals in the coldest sea, and an aboleth's mucus is infamous; with frog slime and a dab of ooze, nothing can get a grip on you.

items.name: Philter of Love
items.effect: The next creature you see within 10 minutes of drinking charms you for 1 hour — and if it's a creature you could fall for, you're smitten while it lasts.

recipe.lore: Rose-coloured and sweet, with a single heart-shaped bubble. Lover's rose is the honest ingredient; an incubus's lips or a lamia's heart are for brewers with fewer scruples.

items.name: Elixir of Health
items.effect: Cures any disease and ends the blinded, deafened, paralyzed and poisoned conditions. The clear red liquid glitters with specks of light.

recipe.lore: Shavings of unicorn horn purify any poison in the cup; feverfew breaks fever and a vulture's gizzard — immune to every rot it swallows — does the rest.

items.name: Restorative Ointment
items.effect: A small jar holding 1d4 + 1 doses of minty salve. Swallowing or rubbing on a dose restores 2d8 + 2 hit points and cures poison and disease.

recipe.lore: Knotwood mends the trees it grows on and bloodwood sap clots like living blood; worked into beeswax with aloe and willow bark and packed into a small clay pot, the salve smells cool and sharp, like crushed mint.

items.name: Universal Solvent
items.effect: A tube of milky liquid that dissolves any adhesive it touches — including sovereign glue — within a round.

recipe.lore: An ancient dragon's acid is too fierce to store, but diluted with pudding acid and ooze-salt it becomes selective: it hungers only for the bonds between things.

items.name: Sovereign Glue
items.effect: Milk-white glue that permanently bonds any two objects after a minute of setting. Only universal solvent, etherealness oil or a wish can part them. Holds 1d6 + 1 ounces.

recipe.lore: A kraken's suckers never let go of a ship; boiled down with mimic adhesive and roper strands, the glue inherits that grip forever. A dose of oil of slipperiness lines the bottle, or the glue seals itself shut.

items.name: Dust of Disappearance
items.effect: A pinch thrown in the air turns you and everyone within 10 feet invisible for 2d4 minutes; attacking or casting ends it for that creature.

recipe.lore: Invisible stalker glass is ground finer than flour; mistcap spores carry it on the air, and silver dust makes it cling to everyone nearby rather than drift away.

items.name: Dust of Dryness
items.effect: Each pinch soaks up a cube of open water up to 15 feet on a side, leaving a marble-sized pellet that releases it all when smashed. A water creature it strikes takes heavy damage.

recipe.lore: A water elemental's core wants to gather water back to itself. Ground with natron — the embalmer's desiccant — it drinks lakes and folds them into a pebble.

items.name: Dust of Sneezing and Choking
items.effect: Looks exactly like dust of disappearance. Once thrown, everyone within 30 feet must save (DC 15 Con) or be unable to breathe and helpless with fits of choking.

recipe.lore: Vrock spores choke the lungs of anything that breathes them. Silver dust gives the mix the same glitter as its innocent cousin — the whole point of the trap.

items.name: Bead of Force
items.effect: Thrown up to 60 feet, this black glass bead bursts for 5d4 force damage and traps everything nearby in a sphere of force for 1 minute.

recipe.lore: Molten glass is quenched in the fluid of a bronze dragon's repulsion gland; the pent-up push inside the bead is what bursts outward into a shell.

items.name: Assassin's Blood
items.effect: (Ingested) The victim takes 1d12 poison damage and is poisoned for a day unless they make a DC 10 Con save (half damage, no poisoning).

recipe.lore: Tasteless in wine, which is why it's the professional's first choice. Hemlock root thickens it; deathcap gives it the kick.

items.name: Burnt Othur Fumes
items.effect: (Inhaled) Victims save (DC 13 Con) or take 3d6 poison damage and must repeat the save each turn, taking 1d6 more on each failure until three saves succeed.

recipe.lore: Othur is a paste of demon stench and brimstone that is burned, not drunk. The sulfur makes it smoulder slowly enough to fill a room.

items.name: Crawler Mucus
items.effect: (Contact) Save (DC 13 Con) or be poisoned and paralyzed for 1 minute, repeating the save each turn.

recipe.lore: The venom is named for the carrion-eating cave crawlers that secrete it; poisoners without one to milk use a chuul's paralytic tentacles instead — cut with ghoul spit and stiffweed, the result is indistinguishable.

items.name: Drow Poison
items.effect: (Injury) Save (DC 13 Con) or be poisoned for 1 hour; fail by 5 or more and you also fall unconscious until you take damage or are shaken awake.

recipe.lore: The underdark recipe is a secret, but surface poisoners get close with couatl venom or slumberlily, stretched with sprite-arrow sap.

items.name: Essence of Ether
items.effect: (Inhaled) Save (DC 15 Con) or be poisoned for 8 hours and unconscious while poisoned, until damaged or shaken awake.

recipe.lore: Dreamfruit rind is dried and powdered with poppy so it can be puffed into a sleeper's face; mandrake is the cheaper, nastier substitute.

items.name: Malice
items.effect: (Inhaled) Save (DC 15 Con) or be poisoned for 1 hour and blinded while poisoned.

recipe.lore: Gloom-moss drinks light where it grows; its dried spores, stirred with darkmantle ink and belladonna, draw a curtain over the victim's eyes.

items.name: Midnight Tears
items.effect: (Ingested) Does nothing until the stroke of midnight. Then, unless neutralized first, the victim saves (DC 17 Con) or takes 9d6 poison damage (half on a success).

recipe.lore: Moonpetal only opens at midnight, and the tears won't 'open' either until that hour. Black lotus supplies the deadliness.

items.name: Oil of Taggit
items.effect: (Contact) Save (DC 13 Con) or be poisoned for 24 hours and unconscious while poisoned; damage wakes the victim.

recipe.lore: Night hags lull their prey with a touch; their fingernail parings, steeped in oil with bellshade, work through the skin just the same.

items.name: Pale Tincture
items.effect: (Ingested) Save (DC 16 Con) or take 1d6 poison damage and be poisoned; the save repeats every 24 hours, dealing another 1d6 poison damage on each failure, and the damage can't heal until the poison ends after seven successful saves.

recipe.lore: Hag's-finger fungus rots whatever it touches; it's cut with tomb mold and — perversely — feverfew, which keeps the victim alive and suffering longer.

items.name: Purple Worm Poison
items.effect: (Injury) Save (DC 19 Con) or take 12d6 poison damage, half as much on a success.

recipe.lore: Only a purple worm will do. The stinger's venom is dangerous to harvest and more dangerous to render; a wyvern barb is used to test each batch on rats.

items.name: Serpent Venom
items.effect: (Injury) Save (DC 11 Con) or take 3d6 poison damage, half as much on a success.

recipe.lore: Common snake venom is concentrated over days until it's as potent as a single drop from a medusa's hair or a naga's gland — which some poisoners simply use instead.

items.name: Torpor
items.effect: (Ingested) Save (DC 15 Con) or be poisoned for 4d6 hours, incapacitated for the whole time.

recipe.lore: A stone golem's lethargy stone slows everything around it; scraped into tea with chamomile, it slows the drinker to a standstill.

items.name: Truth Serum
items.effect: (Ingested) Save (DC 11 Con) or be poisoned for 1 hour, unable to knowingly tell a lie.

recipe.lore: Seer's leaf makes falsehood physically uncomfortable to say. Interrogators add eyebright so the subject's eyes water whenever they try.

items.name: Wyvern Poison
items.effect: (Injury) Save (DC 15 Con) or take 7d6 poison damage, half as much on a success.

recipe.lore: Milked straight from a wyvern's tail sac and rendered with the stinger's own residue, then stored in crystal — it eats through lesser glass.

items.name: Spell Scroll (Cantrip)
items.effect: Holds a cantrip. If the spell is on your class list you can read it to cast it without components, then the scroll crumbles; higher-level spells than you can cast require an ability check.

recipe.requires: The scribe must know or have prepared the spell and expends its material components; casting it once per day of work.
recipe.lore: The ink does the real work — each grade can hold only so much of a spell's weight before the letters smoke. Sand blots the lines; cheap vellum is fine for small magic.

items.name: Giant Boar Roast
items.effect: One serving takes an hour to eat. For the next 8 hours you have temporary hit points equal to your proficiency bonus.

recipe.lore: The heart is slow-roasted in the belly of the joint so its stubborn vigour bastes the meat — boar hunters swear they can take a tusk to the ribs the morning after.

items.name: Hunter's Jerky
items.effect: Keeps for a month and counts as a day's food. For 8 hours after eating it you have advantage on saves against exhaustion from forced marches or going without sleep.

recipe.lore: Dried strips of heart are layered among the ordinary meat — rangers say a beast's endurance lives in its heart, and a pinch of wakeberry keeps the eyelids up.

items.name: Mammoth-Fat Frostbite Salve
items.effect: Rub it on at dawn: for 8 hours you automatically succeed on saves against extreme cold, and have advantage on saves against being frozen or slowed by cold magic.

recipe.lore: Tundra folk render the fat of beasts that never feel the cold, with a little frost lichen to 'teach' the skin. It smells awful and works wonderfully.

items.name: Ranger's Trail Bread
items.effect: Dense, honeyed and nearly unspoilable. If you eat a slice during a short rest, you regain 1 extra hit point for each Hit Die you spend.

recipe.lore: Baked hard enough to break teeth, the bread is soaked in a stream before eating. Silverleaf or a crumb of manna in the dough is why it heals as it fills.

items.name: Seafarer's Chowder
items.effect: For 8 hours you can hold your breath three times as long as normal and have advantage on checks to swim in rough water.

recipe.lore: Pearl divers' grandmothers simmer a dried sea horse or a swim bladder into the pot, and the kelp's air-pods make the broth fizz on the tongue.

items.name: Nightwatch Broth
items.effect: For 8 hours you have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight in dim light, and you can't be surprised while on watch if you are awake.

recipe.lore: Soldiers of the night watch have always sworn by owl-eye broth. Gloomsight mushrooms do the same job for the squeamish.

items.name: Lionsmane Honey Cakes
items.effect: For 1 hour after eating one, you have advantage on saving throws against being frightened.

recipe.lore: Squires eat them before their first battle. The thistle version is golden and sweet; the lion's-heart version is darker and, reputedly, braver.

items.name: Owlbear Stew
items.effect: A thick, feathery-smelling stew. For 8 hours you have advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks and count as one size larger for carrying and grappling.

recipe.lore: Owlbear eggs are cracked into the stew at the last moment and stirred until they thicken it. Mothers are advised to be several miles away first.
